# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Top picks**

- **Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299).** Runner's World ranks them #1 for clear sound and a comfortable clip-on fit that stays put. WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run. Battery is about 7 hours and the rating is IPX4, so they're not ideal for heavy rain. Runner's World also says Bose plans to release a new pair within a month, so you may want to wait. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) · [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list, listed around $125 at some retailers.** It has 12 hours of battery, an IP55 rating, and physical buttons. WIRED found it has more bass but a bit less clarity than the older OpenRun. Long hair and winter hats can get in the way of the neckband. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) · [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Best for long runs and bad weather: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200.** WIRED's top pick, with 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 dust and water rating. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Budget options**

- **Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 (list $149).** SoundGuys calls it the best open-ear pick overall and best for running. It has strong bass for this category and an IP54 rating. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2.** It has an ear-hook design, IP55 and a 10-hour battery. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon, while Dealectric shows $129.99 ($104 with code AFSC20). That's a big gap, so compare prices before buying. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) · [Buy via Dealectric (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- **JLab Flex Open, about $40-50, or Soundpeats PearlClip Pro, about $50.** Both are low-risk ways to find out whether you like clip-ons. Expect less bass and detail. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) · [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Quick guidance**

- Choose bone conduction (Shokz OpenRun Pro 2) if awareness of traffic matters most.
- Choose clip-ons (Bose, OpenDots 2) if you want fuller sound and wear hats or glasses.
- Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise, so they're weaker in loud traffic. Keep the volume low enough to hear your surroundings.

Prices come from the review pages and change often. I didn't have direct store links for every model, so the review pages above link to retailers.
